content.tldr: Essential Iceberg table maintenance includes data file compaction, snapshot expiration, deleting orphan files, and rewriting manifest files to optimize query planning.
content.simple_explanation: An Iceberg table requires routine maintenance to maintain high query efficiency and avoid storage cost bloat: 1) `rewrite_data_files`: compacts small data files into optimal sizes and sorts data using Z-ordering; 2) `expire_snapshots`: removes old snapshots past the retention window and deletes unreferenced data files; 3) `remove_orphan_files`: purges files left behind in cloud storage by failed tasks; 4) `rewrite_manifests`: merges small manifest files to accelerate query planning.
content.real_world_example: Maintaining an office archive: discarding shredded draft documents, consolidating loose papers into organized ring binders, and cleaning out forgotten folders left in hallway storage.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Running `remove_orphan_files` with a retention threshold shorter than the longest running write job can delete active in-flight files written by concurrent tasks, corrupting the table.
